messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. What matters most is getting a fair share. I haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount, and I don’t want my share used to subsidize it. I want B’s interests heard too, but I can’t decide for her. I’d like us to settle it fairly, without rushing.
Thank you. I’d like to buy the house with my husband, ideally at a family discount. It matters to me to have a home we can make our own. I know C hasn’t agreed, so I’m not sure we can move forward.
Thank you. I’d like my share of the estate to give me a chance to start a dance studio; that’s important to me. I know A wants to buy the house, but C hasn’t agreed, so I’m not sure what will happen.
“Fair share” fits; I wouldn’t say “equal” because the shares haven’t been settled. I want everyone heard, but I can’t speak for B. I don’t have anything else to add about the house or Dad right now.

Yes, that fits. The family house matters, but mostly because I could build a secure, independent life there. By a family discount, I mean making it affordable—not recognition or a set price. I am hesitant about putting pressure on C, since she hasn’t agreed.

Yes, that’s about right. I’d like to be able to get started when things are settled, though I don’t have a particular date in mind. I don’t have strong feelings about keeping the house; I’d just hope my share could help with the studio.
Yes, that fits, and independent advice based on the will makes sense. I still haven’t agreed to A buying at a discount, and I can’t speak for B.

Option 1 at full valuation may not be affordable, and it isn’t the family discount I hoped for. I also don’t know what share, if any, would count toward the price, so I wouldn’t want to assume that. Payment over time might help, but C’s agreement still matters to me.
That could work for me, as long as my share is fair and paid out in money. I’d want the valuation and shares made clear before agreeing to anything. I don’t have a strong attachment to the house.
Yes, that fits. You can ask C about payment over time, as long as it’s just exploring an option and not a commitment.
It would depend on the details. Full independent value matters, and I’d need clear terms that protect my share—especially timing, interest and security—before I could agree.
I’d want to know when the money would be paid. If it came in installments, it might be hard to get the studio started, so I’d need to understand the terms before agreeing.

I’m uncomfortable that a family discount seems off the table. Paying full value over time may help, but it doesn’t make the price affordable for us. I’m willing to explore it once the will and shares are clear.
Yes, that fits. I’d need to see the actual payment amount and timing before I could say whether it would let me get started.
